surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Devils cruise past the Stars
paras: Nico Hischier opened the scoring for the Devils early in the first, and the goal stood after the Stars challenged for goalie interference. The second period was a wild one. Hischier scored his second of the night just 38 seconds into the period to make it 2-0. Midway through the second, Jesper Boqvist made it 3-0, and Jamie Benn and Brenden Dillon dropped the gloves. Justin Hryckowian got the Stars on the board late in the second. Luke Hughes stretched the lead to 4-1, 28 seconds later, and Jack Hughes made it 5-1 with less than seven minutes left.

The Devils carried the play, outshooting the Stars 27-18, and got the result to match. Connor Hellebuyck needed only 17 saves for the Devils, and Casey DeSmith allowed five goals on 27 shots. The Devils moved to 8-4-0 and climbed to second in the Metropolitan, while the Stars fell to 7-4-1, third in the Central.
